newsitem.title: UK: BAe calls for more pro-Europe UK - paper.
newsitem.headline: BAe calls for more pro-Europe UK - paper.

text.p: The chief of British Aerospace Plc, one of the UK's leading exporters, has joined a growing list of leading industrialists in a call for the government to adopt a more pro-European outlook, said The Guardian on Thursday.

Sir Richard Evans, BAe's chief executive, said an isolationist approach by the UK government would have serious consequences for the domestic economy and businesses. The report said Evans was also critical of prime minister John Major's effort to keep Eurosceptic Conservative Party members in check.
"We are very much in favour of being an integral part of Europe. What is important to us is stability of currencies," said Evans in The Guardian.
His comments follow similar sentiments being voiced by corporate giants including Unilever Plc and the Japanese car maker Toyota.
Evans said "It is not good for the UK when you have a (political) leadership not able to exercise an influence in Europe that is recognised by other Europeans."
He described a single European currency as "pretty damn fundamental for European industry." --London newsroom +44 171 5427717
